summary: A runtime-created mission's definition follows its canonically first claim's revision, and yields to a publication of the same mission id, so independent updates converge however they arrive.

replay.detail: Incremental person-work projection now gives the definition the revision and source a full replay gives: the canonically first runtime claim's. A publication of the same mission id replaces a runtime-created definition whichever arrives first, and a runtime claim never replaces a published one, so a full replay and every arrival order agree. A definition projected earlier from a later claim is corrected the next time that run tree is rebuilt or the graph is fully replayed; no new replay trigger is added.

schema.detail: No schema, index, trigger or storage-version change.

rules.detail: Claim admission, person authority, idempotency keys, run state, checkpoint rules and revision history are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: No client schema or API change. Runtime-created mission ids are hash-named, so a publication shares one only when deliberately named; such a published definition is kept, with its revision, state and body.

downtime.detail: No restart or startup migration is required by the change.

manual.detail: No manual database repair or new operational command is required.

recovery.detail: The definition's revision and source change together inside the projecting transaction. Failure rolls both back; revision history rows are unchanged.
